# Lift Model Pack Audit

## Status

Evidence class: derived, provisional. This chapter records the cross-engine
audit of the four lift model packs delivered by LIFT-1 (#11741) so it can be
inventoried. It is the first LIFT-11 (#11751) slice. A later slice adds the
LIFT-4 (#11744) static-hold bar wrench. It is not approved. The
registry blocker `UP-D1-lift-pack-audit-inventory` stays open until UP-D1
inventories the pathway and a human reviews it.

## Purpose

Compare the MuJoCo, OpenSim, Drake and Pinocchio lift packs (back squat,
deadlift, bench press, snatch, clean and jerk) on the same inputs. The audit
reduces each engine's own forward kinematics to bar, hand and foot geometry,
compares the engines pose by pose, checks masses and joint limits against the
biomech parity standard, and derives the list of discrepancies with their
tracking issues. It measures software parity between the packs only. It does
not simulate a lift, and it does not compute joint moments, spine loads or
muscle forces.

## Conventions

- Canonical frame from the parity standard: $+Z$ up, $+X$ forward, $+Y$ left,
  SI units. MuJoCo, Drake and Pinocchio already use it. OpenSim is Y-up, and
  its world vectors are rotated by
  $$R_{os} = \begin{pmatrix} 1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & -1 \\ 0 & 1 & 0
  \end{pmatrix}, \qquad p_{can} = R_{os}\,p_{os}$$
- Inputs are canonical joint angles in radians, applied relative to the
  standard's all-zero pose and mapped to each engine's native coordinate
  names and zero offsets.
- Positions are body-frame origins in the world frame. For an evaluated pose
  the pelvis is placed at $(0, 0, 1)$ m unless the pack's start pose is used.
- Reference lifter: 80 kg, 1.78 m. Bar: 20 kg competition bar plus 50 kg per
  side, 120 kg in total.

## Equations

1. Bar frame. With shaft origin $c$ and sleeve origins $s_L$, $s_R$:
   $$\hat a = \frac{s_L - s_R}{\lVert s_L - s_R \rVert}$$
   The axis is undefined, and the audit raises `ValueError`, when the sleeves
   coincide ($\lVert s_L - s_R \rVert < 10^{-9}$ m). The axis is built from
   the sleeve origins, so a pack's local bar-axis convention does not matter.
2. Hand-to-bar geometry, per side $k \in \{l, r\}$, with hand origin $h_k$ and
   $r_k = h_k - c$:
   $$\ell_k = r_k \cdot \hat a, \qquad
     d_k = \lVert r_k - \ell_k\,\hat a \rVert$$
   $\ell_k$ is the signed lateral offset along the bar (positive toward the
   left sleeve) and $d_k$ the perpendicular distance to the bar axis. A hand
   that grips the bar has $d_k \approx 0$. A back-squat bar rides on the back,
   so $d_k \approx 0.59$ m is expected there.
3. Placement-independent pose summary. With the foot midpoint
   $f = \tfrac{1}{2}(p_{foot,l} + p_{foot,r})$, the bar centre and hand
   positions are reported as $c - f$ and $h_k - f$. The grip width is
   $\lVert h_l - h_r \rVert$.
4. Same-input parity. For a body $b$ in pose $q$ the pelvis-relative position
   is $\rho_b = p_b - p_{pelvis}$. For an engine pair $(i, j)$ and a body set
   $B$:
   $$\Delta_B = \max_{b \in B} \lVert \rho_b^{(i)} - \rho_b^{(j)} \rVert_\infty$$
   It is evaluated for the segment origins, the hands, the feet and the bar
   centre, and reported as the worst value over all engine pairs and poses.
   The pose set is the standard's zero, flexion, frontal and axial poses plus
   four generic lift shapes (hip hinge, front rack, overhead, squat bottom).
   None of these is any pack's own phase data.
5. Lifter-only centre of mass. The bar and bench links have zero mass-centre
   offset in every pack, so with total mass $M$, whole-model CoM $x_G$ and
   removed links $e$ of mass $m_e$ at origin $p_e$:
   $$x_{lifter} = \frac{M\,x_G - \sum_e m_e\,p_e}{M - \sum_e m_e} - p_{pelvis}$$
   It is unavailable when no lifter mass remains.
6. Segment mass deviation, against the standard's segment mass $m^{std}_s$ at
   its standard body mass $M^{std}$, scaled to the lifter mass $M_L$:
   $$\varepsilon_s = \frac{\left| m_s - m^{std}_s\,M_L / M^{std} \right|}
     {m^{std}_s\,M_L / M^{std}}$$
7. Joint limits. A native limit $[\underline q, \overline q]$ with zero
   offset $o$ is compared in canonical angles as
   $\max\left(|\underline q - o - \underline q^{std}|,
   |\overline q - o - \overline q^{std}|\right)$.
8. Grip width. The intended half-width is $|\ell_l|$ at the zero pose and the
   achievable half-spacing is $\tfrac{1}{2}\lVert h_l - h_r \rVert$ at the same
   pose. The mismatch is their difference.
9. Start pose. The sole height $z_{sole}$ is the lowest point of the foot
   contact geometry: MuJoCo and Pinocchio foot boxes, OpenSim contact-sphere
   surfaces, and the lowest Drake foot sole corner. The bar height above the sole is
   $c_z - z_{sole}$. For floor pulls (deadlift, snatch, clean and jerk) its
   target is the 0.225 m plate radius of a 450 mm plate.
10. Reference FK. Each engine's pelvis-relative origins are compared with the
    standard's reference FK scaled to the lifter height, as the worst
    component difference over the common segments. It is not evaluated for
    the bench press.

## Tolerances and Thresholds

| Quantity | Value | Source |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Cross-engine position | 0.02 m | parity standard `cross_engine_position_abs_m` |
| Mass | $10^{-6}$ relative | parity standard `mass_rel` |
| Joint limit | $10^{-4}$ rad | parity standard `limit_abs_rad` |
| Grip mismatch and native start closure | 0.01 m | audit threshold |
| Floor-pull bar height | 0.225 m $\pm$ 0.05 m | 450 mm plate radius, audit threshold |

The audit thresholds flag discrepancies for tracking. They are not acceptance
limits for a lift simulation.

## Discrepancy Derivation

`derive_gaps` computes every discrepancy from the measured rows. None is
entered by hand. The classes are: grip attachment, grip width, start pose,
joint limits, phase count, left-only phase targets, phase keys that do not
resolve to model coordinates, bench mass convention, start-pose contact force,
segment inertia and missing ground reaction. Each class maps to the per-pack
issues in the model repositories and to the LIFT child of epic #11740 expected
to close it.

## Unavailable Values

- Drake and Pinocchio packs expose no contact model, so start-pose ground
  contact force is unavailable with a reason, never zero.
- Native hand-to-bar closure is reported only where the engine defines it
  (MuJoCo welds, OpenSim weld constraint after assembly). It is unavailable
  for Drake and Pinocchio.
- The lifter-only CoM is unavailable when no lifter mass remains, and the bar
  height is unavailable when no foot contact geometry is found.
- Missing bodies, non-finite positions and coincident sleeves raise
  `ValueError`. No geometric value is filled in.

The geometry, frame and analysis functions are engine-independent numpy over
plain data. The adapters load each pack and supply canonical body origins,
masses, coordinates, contact force and closure.

## Recorded Baseline

The measured baseline, generated by the runner and not edited by hand, is
`docs/development/lifting/PACK_PARITY_BASELINE.md`, with the receipt
`docs/development/lifting/pack_parity_baseline.json`. It records the pack
commits and engine versions used. Its main findings:

- Segment, hand and foot parity is within the 0.02 m tolerance for every lift
  (worst segment 0.0115 m, OpenSim against Drake at the flexion pose).
- Bar-centre differences reach 0.24 m. They come from the packs' different
  grip offsets, not from forward kinematics.
- The lifter-only CoM differs by up to 0.079 m between MuJoCo and OpenSim at
  the squat-bottom pose, which exceeds the position tolerance.
- The right hand is not attached to the bar in the Drake and Pinocchio packs,
  and the grip half-width does not match the achievable hand spacing in all
  four packs.
- No floor-pull start pose places the bar at the plate radius.

## Static-Hold Bar Wrench

Evidence class: derived, provisional (LIFT-4 #11744 scope 3, MuJoCo slice).
The registry blocker `UP-D1-lift-bar-hold-wrench-inventory` stays open until
the pathway is inventoried and reviewed.

The question is what force each hand exerts on the bar when the lifter holds
the pack's start pose still. It is answered for the MuJoCo pack only. The
other packs report it unavailable until their slices land.

### Method

1. Rigid lifter. On a private copy of the model, every degree of freedom that
   does not belong to a body whose name starts with `barbell` gets
   `dof_armature` $= 10^{9}$. The lifter therefore cannot accelerate under the
   bar load. Only the bar moves.
2. No support but the hands. Every barbell geom gets `contype` and
   `conaffinity` 0, so the floor, rack or bench never carries the load.
3. Settled hold. From the pack's first keyframe (else `qpos0`) at zero
   velocity, the model is stepped for $T_s = 1$ s, then `mj_forward` is
   called. The pack welds use MuJoCo's default `solref` time constant of
   0.02 s, so $T_s$ is 50 time constants. A single `mj_forward` from rest is
   not used, because it reports only the impedance-scaled first-instant
   constraint force, about 5 % short of the weight at the default `solimp`.
4. Per-hand wrench. For each hand-to-bar weld $k \in \{L, R\}$ the equality
   rows of `efc_force` are mapped to a world-frame wrench $(F_k, \tau_k)$ on
   the bar at the bar-side anchor $p_k$, by the GCV-8 extraction
   (`grip_efc.py`). The sign follows ADR-0052:
   the wrench is the one exerted by the hand on the bar, so a held bar has
   $F_{k,z} > 0$. The GCV-7 grip reduction (`grip_wrench.py`) then forms the
   couple. No second wrench-transport routine is used.

### Equations

11. Bar weight, with $m_{bar}$ the summed mass of the `barbell` bodies:
    $$W = m_{bar}\,\lVert g \rVert$$
    $m_{bar} \le 0$ or $\lVert g \rVert \le 0$ raises `ValueError`.
12. Static equilibrium residual:
    $$\varepsilon_W = \frac{\left| F_{L,z} + F_{R,z} - W \right|}{W}$$
13. Left-hand share of the vertical load:
    $$s_L = \frac{F_{L,z}}{F_{L,z} + F_{R,z}}$$
    It raises `ValueError` when $|F_{L,z} + F_{R,z}| < 10^{-9}$ N.
14. Couple about the anchor midpoint $m = \tfrac{1}{2}(p_L + p_R)$:
    $$C = \sum_k (p_k - m) \times F_k + \sum_k \tau_k$$
    The anchor is the weld's bar-side site, else the bar body origin. With
    body-to-body welds both anchors are the bar body origin, so $m$ is that
    origin and $C = \tau_L + \tau_R$.
15. Rest check. The bar's residual world-frame linear acceleration is
    $$a_{bar} = \max_{b} \lVert a^{prop}_b + g \rVert$$
    over the `barbell` bodies, where $a^{prop}_b$ is the proper acceleration
    from `mj_rnePostConstraint` and `mj_objectAcceleration`. It is reported,
    so the static-hold assumption is checked rather than assumed.

### Acceptance and Measured Values

| Quantity | Acceptance | Source |
| --- | --- | --- |
| $\varepsilon_W$ | $\le 0.01$ | #11744 acceptance |
| $\lvert s_L - 0.5 \rvert$, symmetric grip | $\le 10^{-6}$ | test tolerance |
| $a_{bar}$ | $< 10^{-3}$ m/s² | test tolerance |

Measured on MuJoCo_Models `284b9b2` with the 120 kg reference bar (desk-lead,
PR #12189): for the deadlift, bench press, snatch and clean and jerk,
$\varepsilon_W \le 3.3 \times 10^{-7}$, $\lvert s_L - 0.5 \rvert \le
3 \times 10^{-16}$ and $a_{bar} \le 3.3 \times 10^{-6}$ m/s². The back
squat is unavailable, because its bar is welded to the torso.

### Unavailable Cases

Each case returns `available: false`, a reason, and `None` in every numeric
field, never zero:

- No hand-to-bar weld for one or both hands. The reason names the bodies the
  bar is attached to instead, for example the torso in the back squat.
- No `barbell` body has a joint. The bar is then fixed to the world, its
  weight never enters the dynamics and no weld reaction can carry it.
- The weld reaction for a hand cannot be extracted, for example an inactive
  weld or a rank-deficient weld Jacobian.
- The engine adapter has no implementation. This is the base-class default
  and applies to OpenSim, Drake and Pinocchio for now.

### Limitations

- Two welds on one rigid bar make the hold statically indeterminate. Only
  the total vertical force is fixed by equilibrium. The left/right split, the
  horizontal forces and the free torques come from MuJoCo's soft-constraint
  regularization, which gives equal impedance to both welds. They are not a
  prediction of how a lifter shares the load. $s_L = 0.5$ for a symmetric
  grip confirms symmetry of the model, not physiology.
- The lifter is held rigid by armature, so no joint moment, muscle force or
  spine load follows from this result. The hold is the start pose only, not
  a lift trajectory.
- The weld reaction includes no grip compliance, friction or slip.
- No force-instrumented bar data exist. The values are software results,
  validated only against the bar's own weight.

## Tests and Reproduction

```bash
python3 -m pytest tests/unit/lifting/pack_audit/test_pack_audit_geometry.py \
  tests/unit/lifting/pack_audit/test_pack_audit_frames_names.py \
  tests/unit/lifting/pack_audit/test_pack_audit_report.py \
  tests/unit/lifting/pack_audit/test_bar_hold_wrench.py -q
```

These tests check the bar frame, hand-bar metrics and pose summary on
constructed positions, and the frame rotations and name mappings. The report
tests check the committed receipt: every lift and engine is covered, FK parity
holds except for the bar, every derived gap maps to an issue in a known
repository, and the committed Markdown matches the receipt. They need no
engine.
`test_pack_audit_live.py` runs the adapters against checked-out packs and
skips when the packs or engines are absent.
`test_bar_hold_wrench.py` checks the static-hold bar wrench on a two-hand
MuJoCo fixture (weight balance, even split, bar at rest, upward hand force),
the torso-weld and world-fixed-bar cases (unavailable, every numeric field
`None`), and the four hand-held lifts of the MuJoCo pack. The fixture and pack
cases need MuJoCo, and the pack cases also need a MuJoCo pack checkout (for
example under `LIFT_PACK_ROOT`); they skip otherwise. Regenerate the baseline with
`python3 scripts/lifting/run_pack_parity_baseline.py`, with the four pack
checkouts found under `LIFT_PACK_ROOT`.

## Assumptions and Limitations

- The audit compares body-frame origins. It does not compare geometry
  surfaces, inertia tensors beyond the inertia gap class, or dynamics.
- Bar and bench links are assumed to have zero mass-centre offset, which holds
  for every pack at the recorded commits. The lifter-only CoM is wrong if a
  pack changes that.
- MuJoCo phase values may be absolute positions or reference-relative angles.
  The audit reads them as canonical angles, so MuJoCo phase out-of-range flags
  depend on that reading and are not used as gaps.
- OpenSim start-pose values are after model assembly, which moves coordinates
  off their defaults.
- OpenSim, Drake and Pinocchio stills are skeleton plots of each engine's own
  FK, not native renders.
- No Simscape or MATLAB lift models exist, and nothing was substituted for
  them.
- No lift motion-capture or force-plate data exist. The baseline records
  software parity between packs, not physical validity of any lift, and no
  uncertainty against measured lifts is claimed.
